title: Two-Step Clinical Reasoning in INI-CET-Style Questions
subject: INI-CET Strategy
preview: Integrated clinical questions often require a diagnosis followed by its mechanism, complication or best test.
quickRevision: Integrated clinical questions often require a diagnosis followed by its mechanism, complication or best test.
Check whether two answer choices are both generally true but only one answers the precise task.
A short differential of two or three realistic alternatives is usually more useful than an exhaustive list.

sections.title: Recognize the question type
points: Integrated clinical questions often require a diagnosis followed by its mechanism, complication or best test.
Organize information as presentation, key discriminant, likely mechanism, next decision.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not confuse a disease-associated fact with the most appropriate answer for this patient.

quiz.question: What is a useful two-step reasoning approach?
options: Treat all differentials as equally likely
Recognize the syndrome then identify the specific requested decision
